newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean 3-yr yields end lower on surplus news.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean 3-yr yields end lower on surplus news.

text.p: Yields on three-year benchmark corporate bonds ended sharply lower on Tuesday as cash liquidity was ample and news of South Korea's first monthly trade surplus since December 1994 boosted buying sentiment, dealers said.
Dealers said they expected the corporate bond yield to fall further on Wednesday on stable short-term cash flow and a forecast for fewer new issues following the trade surplus.
* 3-yr corporates closed down at 11.63 vs 11.75 pct
* 3-mth CDs closed down at 11.90 pct vs 12.00
* Overnight average call rate at 11.46 pct vs 11.58 pct
Yields on benchmark three-year corporate bonds ended sharply lower on Tuesday due to active buying following news of South Korea's first monthly trade surplus since December 1994, dealers said.
They said short-term liquidity was good following the end of the first half of the year on Monday, which had made institutions conservative spenders recently.
The central bank on Tuesday siphoned off one trillion won in a one-day repurchase agreement (repo), but traders said it did not affect the market.

Kang Yung-gee at Hyundai Securities also attributed the fall in the benchmark yield to a lower-than-expected volume of new July issues. New applications for South Korean corporate bond issues in July totalled 2.82 trillion won, against June's 2.85 trillion.
This is the first month that the Korea Securities Dealers Association stopped approving corporate bond issues. All applications from July will be accepted.
"We feared a large new number of issues for July but fortunately it is similar to the June issues," said Kang.
A dealer at KDB Securities said he expected fewer new issues of corporate bonds thanks to the monthly trade surplus, which showed the economy was strengthening.
He expected Wednesday's corporate bond yield to fall to 11.50.
